_: Long-form overrides. Inherits brand, voice and content standards from the shorts profile; everything below differs because 8 minutes is not 45 seconds. See MODEL_DEV_LOG_LONGFORM.md.

tts.comment: Same voice as the shorts for channel consistency. Pace is SLOWER than the shorts' 1.18: that number was chosen against 0.7 cuts/sec and a second speaker to play off. Over 8 minutes of continuous narration a fast read becomes exhausting rather than urgent. 1.10 is a starting point and must be judged on a finished cut (F31), not on a sample.

pacing.comment: Long-form cadence from L001: ~0.36 cuts/sec overall, but 35 percent of gaps are sub-second and 2 percent run past 12s. Bursts and holds, same principle as shorts at a different scale (L2).

audio.comment: Long-form convention is quieter than shorts. L001 sits at -18.8 LUFS, which is quiet even for the format; -15 is a better target for YouTube.

overlays.comment: No end card, same reasoning as shorts (F17). Film burns are a shorts device and would be exhausting over 8 minutes — long-form transitions are the date and quote cards instead.

editorial.comment: Long-form is an argument, not a hook. The narration share floor is higher because in this format the narration IS the product — source clips are evidence for claims it makes.
editorial.sourceAudioRule: Let a clip speak only when the fact that THEY said it is the evidence (L5). Front-load source audio in the cold open; the final third carries no source audio at all so nothing competes with the conclusion.
